claims.title: Active-experiment marginal value need not satisfy diminishing returns under one fixed oracle benchmark
claims.scope: finite active fixed-model policy classes B, B+a, B+b, and B+a+b evaluated against one full-menu model-informed causal oracle vector
assumptions: the full-menu oracle benchmark is held fixed across all four controller classes
all exact policy frontier searches complete below configured caps
nonclaims: the theorem does not claim all experiment-value functions are supermodular
the result does not imply greedy selection is always suboptimal
the result is not evidence for simulation

claims.title: Experiment complementarity can persist after independent public-randomness resources are matched
claims.scope: the same four active fixed-model policy classes after source-independent public-seed convexification of complete deterministic policy trees
assumptions: public mixing is available under the same rule for all four policy classes
mixed minimax values are solved by the exact rational zero-sum game
nonclaims: public randomness is an explicit assistance resource
strict complementarity is not guaranteed for every model family

claims.title: Fixed full-menu oracle benchmarking removes menu-dependent oracle motion from experiment-complementarity comparisons
claims.scope: four nested experiment policy classes all evaluated by subtracting one full-menu model-informed oracle vector
assumptions: the full-menu oracle is feasible as a benchmark lower bound for every restricted-menu controller
the same model family, horizon, code universe, and cost accounting are used throughout
nonclaims: this benchmark choice is one declared estimand rather than the only possible notion of experiment value
the oracle is not future-path clairvoyant

claims.title: Negative cost-form submodularity slack is exactly equivalent to positive two-experiment complementarity margin
claims.scope: any four finite policy-class values V(B), V(B+a), V(B+b), and V(B+a+b) under the declared minimization convention
assumptions: marginal gain is defined as V(S)-V(S+e)
nonclaims: the algebraic equivalence does not establish the sign of the slack in arbitrary problems

claims.title: Two persistent latent bits give deterministic K3 complementarity margin one
claims.scope: four globally fixed two-period models indexed by two latent bits, K3 source mapping 0,1,1,2 in the second period, and one experiment revealing each bit
assumptions: the first-period source is common and known
each bit observation persists through the public history
the full-menu oracle cost is two for every model
nonclaims: the unit margin is specific to this exact finite construction

claims.title: The two-bit K3 complementarity margin remains one-third after public-seed convexification
claims.scope: the same persistent two-bit K3 construction after independent public mixing over complete deterministic policies
assumptions: baseline mixed benchmark gap is two-thirds
the both-bit mixed gap is zero
nonclaims: the one-third value is not a universal interaction coefficient

claims.title: Bounded exact active-experiment complementarity audit
claims.scope: two-bit K3 deterministic and public-mixed complementarity, experiment-order symmetry, fixed full-menu oracle, exact game duality, and candidate-name validation
assumptions: all active policy frontiers, singleton oracles, and zero-sum support searches complete below configured caps
all probabilities and costs use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded exact checks are not a continuous-model or scalability theorem
CI success is not empirical evidence for simulation
